chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It suffices you that, if you are with them, from the recitation, [it is] like the recitation of the self [i.e., individual recitation]."

key_terms.حَدِيثِ النَّفْسِ: Individual/Personal recitation (as opposed to congregational or loud recitation)
key_terms.يُجْزِيكَ: It suffices you / It is valid for you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a follower's Quran recitation during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a follower (muqtadi) who is reciting Quran behind an Imam, establishing that their individual recitation is sufficient (yujzi) rather than requiring strict synchronization or total silence. This supports the view that recitation is a personal obligation of the follower, allowing them to continue their own recitation even while the Imam is reciting aloud or silently, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the relationship between the Imam's and the follower's recitation.
